column2: On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Every joint of a person owes a charity every day on which the sun rises. Judging justly between two people is a charity;

helping a man with his mount, lifting him onto it or lifting his belongings onto it, is a charity; a good word is a charity; every step you take towards the prayer is a charity; and removing something harmful from the road is a charity.” Reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

His words, “Every joint (sulāmā) of a person owes a charity every day on which the sun rises”: al-sulāmā are the joints, which number three hundred and sixty, as explained in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim in the hadith of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) (1007).
The meaning is that every day on which the sun rises, all those joints owe a charity on that day. Then he mentioned examples of things by which charity is achieved,

some of them actions and some words, some limited to the doer and some extending to others. In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, in the hadith of Abū Dharr (720), he says: “Two rakʿahs that he prays in the forenoon (ḍuḥā) suffice for that,”
because in praying these two rakʿahs the joints move in this act of worship, the prayer, so they suffice in place of the charities for that day.
Every act of devotion a person performs, whether in word or deed, is a charity. What the Prophet ﷺ mentioned in this hadith is by way of example, not limitation.

Judging justly between two people may be in giving a ruling or in reconciling two disputing parties with justice; this is a word whose benefit extends to others. Helping a man by lifting him onto his mount or lifting his belongings onto it is a deed whose benefit extends to others.

Saying a good word includes all good speech: remembrance [of Allah], supplication, recitation, teaching, enjoining good, forbidding evil and so on; it is a word whose benefit is both limited to the doer and extends to others.

Every step a Muslim takes towards the prayer is a charity from the Muslim to himself; it is a deed limited to the doer. Removing something harmful from the road—a thorn, a stone, glass and the like—is a deed whose benefit extends to others.
Every joint of a person owes a charity every day, whether one limited to the doer or extending to others.
The hadith encourages reconciling disputing parties with justice.
A Muslim is urged to help others with what they need, such as lifting someone onto his mount or lifting his belongings onto it.
All good speech is encouraged: remembrance [of Allah], recitation, teaching, calling [to Allah] and so on.
Walking to the mosques has great virtue; another hadith says that the walker's steps there and back are recorded for him (reported by Muslim, 663).
Removing harmful things from the road has great virtue; another hadith says that it is one of the branches of faith (reported by Muslim, 58).
